title: NASA Glenn's examples of the third law are a wing and a jet engine
summary: The page says a wing deflects air downward and the air pushes the wing upward, and that a jet's exhaust goes back while the thrust goes forward.
body: On the same Newton's-laws page, NASA Glenn gives two aerodynamic examples of the third law. For lift: the air is deflected downward by the airfoil's action, and in reaction the wing is pushed upward. For a jet engine: hot exhaust gases flow out the back, and a thrusting force is produced in the opposite direction. These are the page's illustrations of 'equal and opposite', not a full derivation of lift. The Bernoulli page is a different account of pressure and speed along a streamline. The two pages were both opened. This shard does not merge them into one mechanism.
